```text
Check if this issue is valid — if so, understand the root cause and fix it. When an issue isn't valid or won't be fixed in this PR, reply in its thread with the reason and then resolve the thread. At internal/providers/mistral/finish.go, line 25:

<comment>The byte precheck skips valid JSON encodings of `model_length`, so clients can still receive the unknown finish reason. Make the fast path escape-aware, or parse whenever the payload contains an escape.</comment>

<file context>
@@ -0,0 +1,61 @@
+// returns the original data untouched when the marker is absent, and reports
+// whether a rewrite happened.
+func mapFinishReasons(data []byte) ([]byte, bool) {
+	if !bytes.Contains(data, modelLengthMarker) {
+		return data, false
+	}
</file context>
```

</details>

** Minor** · **Functional Correctness** · **Quick win** **Allow Unicode-escaped finish reasons through the byte check.** JSON permits `"model\u005flength"` as a representation of `"model_length"`. ([rfc-editor.org](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8259.html)) This payload contains no literal `model_length`, so Line 25 skips normalization. Both response paths can therefore return the unmapped finish reason. When the literal marker is absent but Unicode escapes are present, fall back to JSON parsing. Add an escaped-value regression case alongside the literal-value tests. Based on learnings, raw JSON scans can miss Unicode-escaped names; the same limitation applies to this value scan.
